formationLabel: Lithuanian congregation established August 24, 1918 · changed from personal to territorial parish April 8, 1959 · merged into St. Francis of Assisi Parish July 1, 2013
currentUse: The former St. George church at 3121 Sheridan Avenue is standing and used by New Birth Missionary Baptist Church. St. George's Roman Catholic institutional life ended in the July 1, 2013 merger that formed St. Francis of Assisi Parish; the later building sale and reuse are separate events.
summary: St. George was Saginaw's Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish, established as a separate congregation on August 24, 1918 after Lithuanian Catholics had worshiped at Polish St. Casimir. A canonical decree converted it from an ethnic personal parish to a territorial parish on April 8, 1959. Its later church at 3121 Sheridan Avenue was completed in 1964. St. George merged with St. Anthony and St. Casimir on July 1, 2013 to form St. Francis of Assisi Parish; the former church was subsequently sold and remains in use by New Birth Missionary Baptist Church.

institutionLifecycle.formation: Lithuanian Catholics first worshiped at St. Casimir Polish Parish. A separate St. George congregation of sixty families was established on August 24, 1918.
institutionLifecycle.institutionalForm: Lithuanian Roman Catholic personal or ethnic parish from 1918; converted by canonical decree into a territorial parish on April 8, 1959 without creating a new institution.
institutionLifecycle.terminalStatus: St. George, St. Anthony, and St. Casimir merged on July 1, 2013 to establish the distinct St. Francis of Assisi Parish. A later 2015 date belongs to the former church's sale or end of Catholic site use, not the parish merger.
institutionLifecycle.currentVerification: The successor parish's history establishes the 2013 merger. Saginaw municipal records from 2018 and a 2026 Saginaw County election notice identify New Birth Missionary Baptist Church at 3121 Sheridan Avenue, verifying later non-Catholic use of the standing building.

historicalNarrative.text: Lithuanian Catholics in Saginaw initially worshiped at the distinct Polish St. Casimir Parish. On August 24, 1918, a separate St. George congregation was established with sixty families. The shared early host does not make the two parishes the same institution.

sources.locator: Wolkovich, Lithuanian Religious Life in America, Vol. 3, printed pp. 96-97

historicalNarrative.text: St. George began as a Lithuanian personal or ethnic parish. As enrollment remained small, the Diocese of Saginaw converted it by canonical decree into a territorial parish on April 8, 1959. This was a change in canonical and pastoral form within the same institution, not closure or replacement.

sources.locator: Wolkovich, Lithuanian Religious Life in America, Vol. 3, printed pp. 97-98, April 8, 1959 decree

historicalNarrative.text: The parish's first church stood near South Jefferson and Wisner streets according to attributed field history and no longer survives. Because the exact parcel and demolition date are unresolved, this site is kept separate from the later Sheridan Avenue church.

historicalNarrative.text: Ground was broken for a replacement church on May 5, 1963, and the building was completed on Ash Wednesday 1964. A 2009 Saginaw polling-place list identifies the active St. George Church at 3121 Sheridan Avenue, independently anchoring the later worship site and address.

sources.locator: Wolkovich, Lithuanian Religious Life in America, Vol. 3, printed p. 98

historicalNarrative.text: St. George's institutional life ended on July 1, 2013 when it merged with St. Anthony and St. Casimir to establish St. Francis of Assisi Parish. The successor parish's own history supplies that date and named three predecessor institutions. A secondary 2015 closure reading instead corresponds to the former building's later sale or end of Catholic use and is not used as the parish's terminal date.

sources.locator: History section, St. Francis of Assisi established July 1, 2013 from St. George, St. Anthony, and St. Casimir
Saginaw St. George section, attributed 2015 building sale/closure reading

historicalNarrative.text: The Sheridan Avenue church remains standing in non-Catholic religious use. A 2018 city agenda and a 2026 Saginaw County election notice both place New Birth Missionary Baptist Church at 3121 Sheridan Avenue. This later building use is not a canonical successor relationship to St. George, and no claim is made about the interior or structural condition.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: The 1959 date is a canonical transition from personal to territorial parish, not closure. The parish's institutional end occurred in the July 1, 2013 merger that formed St. Francis of Assisi. The attributed 2015 reading belongs to the later building sale or end of Catholic site use and must not replace the 2013 institutional event.
gaps: The exact address and parcel of the early church; its construction and demolition dates; the Sheridan Avenue church's dedication date; the 2013 merger decree and exact records custody; the precise 2015 sale instrument and date; any cemetery; and the former church's interior and structural condition remain unresolved.
